blocks.x: Regulated token designs: legal-wrapper-first architecture, transfer controls that enforce restrictions in code, ledger and cap-table reconciliation at zero delta — and every lifecycle event from issuance to redemption designed before the token exists.
The token is the easy part — the legal wrapper is the product
blocks.sub: Wrapper-first tokenization: rights drafted, registers synced, settlement timed

blocks.x: Tokenization succeeds or fails on the legal design: what is the token legally, who may hold it, how do transfers respect securities law, and what happens in a default? The engineering implements the lawyers' decisions as transfer controls — allow-lists, lockups, jurisdiction checks — enforced in code, not in prospectus fine print.

The practice covers wrapper selection, token standards with compliant behavior, issuer and transfer-agent integration, and settlement workflows that shorten cycles where the law permits and document where it does not.
Below: the failure modes that strand tokenized assets, the reference architecture of wrapper-first design, and the console that keeps the ledger reconciled to reality.

widgets.title: Corporate-action workflow — click each stage for its duty

stages.name: Event intake
stages.detail: Corporate actions arrive as typed objects (coupon, redemption, split, freeze) with legal references attached; an action without its instrument reference cannot enter the workflow.

stages.name: Eligibility
stages.detail: Snapshot at record date from the ledger-of-record with jurisdiction fences applied; eligibility disputes resolve against the snapshot, not against memory.

stages.name: Computation
stages.detail: Amounts computed per holding with rounding policy explicit; the computation artifact is retained — a holder query in year 5 gets the exact numbers from the run.

stages.name: Execution
stages.detail: Payouts execute under custody quorum with dual-control review; frozen holdings are excluded and reported, never silently skipped.

stages.name: Reconcile
stages.detail: Post-execution reconciliation against the registrar of record; a delta of any size blocks the next lifecycle event until explained.

widgets.note: The five stages are the duty chain — notification, computation, execution and reconciliation each leave evidence a regulator can read.

widgets.title: Custody control bands — quorum, cold share, recovery readiness
widgets.note: Gauges show each custody control against its band. Recovery drill recency is the one that slips in every program — the band turns it into a scheduled obligation.

widgets.title: Transfer-restriction what-if — fences, lockups and liquidity
widgets.note: Fences fragment liquidity: each added jurisdiction thins the order book — the curve is the argument for choosing the wrapper's jurisdiction set before marketing promises liquidity.

Delivery-versus-payment is a legal statement
blocks.sub: Timed legs, reconciliation gates and the register of record — the mechanics that make tokenized assets real

blocks.x: Tokenization becomes real when the off-chain register, the on-ledger token and the custody arrangement agree — every day, provably. The settlement workflow therefore runs as delivery-versus-payment with timed legs: the cash leg and the asset leg are enforced by the contract, the reconciliation gate compares ledger holdings against the transfer agent's register daily, and any break is a stop-the-world event, not a ticket. Transfer controls enforce eligibility before every movement — whitelists, duty checks and jurisdiction matrices evaluated at the contract boundary — so a restricted transfer fails by construction rather than by after-the-fact clawback.

The lifecycle is rehearsed before issuance: corporate actions, splits, redemptions and holder-noticing run as drills against a staging network with the real wrapper documents, because the failure modes that strand tokenized assets are always lifecycle events nobody scheduled. The console's headline is reconciliation, not volume — a tokenization program with daily zero-break reconciliation is sellable to auditors; one with impressive TPS is not.

items: Cash and asset legs enforced by contract; settlement is atomic or it does not happen.
Ledger versus register versus custody; zero breaks is the operating standard.

How do you keep a token legally enforceable across jurisdictions?

The legal wrapper is designed first: the token encodes the wrapper’s transfer restrictions in code, and the charter maps on-chain roles to off-chain legal obligations. Regulators read the wrapper; the code enforces it.
What stops a restricted token from falling into the wrong hands?

Transfer controls run at the token layer: eligibility predicates, holding limits and jurisdiction rules execute on every transfer attempt. A non-compliant transfer fails in code, and the attempt is logged for the compliance file.
Can this integrate with our existing transfer agent and registries?

Yes — the integration surface names registries, transfer agents and settlement rails explicitly. The token layer reconciles against the registers rather than replacing them wherever the wrapper requires a register of record.
What happens at corporate actions — dividends, redemptions, splits?

Lifecycle events are governed by the same wrapper: the overlay schedules them, executes against the cap-table state and produces the evidence pack the asset-ops team reconciles — no manual spreadsheet pass at each event.
How quickly can we see settlement improve?
The chart is the design target: 1–2 day cycles across the listed asset classes, with the previous cycle shown honestly. The gates before issuance prove the transfer controls before volume moves.
